seeing this shearing of the mourning hair

Phylarchus says that Aeschylus (fr. 322) relates that the Curetes got their name because of their luxury. More on this name and its accent, which varies in the manuscripts (Κούρητες [Curetes] or Κουρήτες [Curetes]), see in Thes. vol. 4 p. 1891.
and a lock of hair luxuriant as on delicate maidens, whence they approved calling the people Curetes
to relate that they got their name because of their luxury
he sent a shorn lock of hair for his father's sake
about the feast of Thyestes, about which likewise Ch. 1068 παιδοβόροι μὲν πρῶτον ὑπῆρξαν μόχθοι τάλανές τε Θυέστου [child-devouring were the first woes, and the wretched ones of Thyestes].
child-devouring were the first woes, and the wretched ones of Thyestes
he leaped a light leap from the ship
if you would grant me a light fulfillment of my request
you accomplished your former need from me lightly
and these things he sprang lightly from the midst of the nets
may the wind shake the earth from its foundations with its very roots
but you have shrieked and are moaning?
but now I have not yet cried out the noble strain
where κράναι [to accomplish] is an optative, taken as an infinitive by an interpolator who after τερπνά [delightful] added τούτων αἰτεῖ [asks for these things], which I deleted.
where κρανοῖτο [it might be accomplished] is more probable, which Elmsley restored.
not yet has fate, the fulfiller, ordained to accomplish these things in this way
and he threatens the towers with terrible things which fortune may not accomplish
he threatens these towers with things which a god may not accomplish
accomplishing the ancient evil counsels of Laius
fair tokens of Zeus, daughter, to accomplish delightful things
but if the god accomplishes the opposite
O gods, accomplish justly the judgments
where will it end, where will the fury of ruin cease after it has been lulled to rest?
by the grace of Pallas and Loxias and of the third savior who accomplishes all things
but I would not accomplish my promise before
he accomplished these things without a summoner, so that they are
of which this vote is being accomplished
he had prophesied the future, whether it might be accomplished
then the curse of Cronus will be completely accomplished
how has it been accomplished in the house?
these lots were accomplished upon us
if the matter is accomplished perfectly
one vote, publicly enacted from the city, has been accomplished
Cranaus, most ancient king of the Athenians
Cranaus, most ancient king of the Athenians
i.e. the Athenians, who are also called Kpavaoi: see Thes. vol. 4 p. 1915.
Nauck thinks that Aeschylus Eum. 1011 πολισσούχοι παῖδες Κραναοῦ [city-holding children of Cranaus] is referred to.
